notes:
## 2.27.1
- A maintenance release: 2.27.0 rebuilt from the merged source, which also carries every 2.26.x change. Nothing changes for games.

## Engine UI
- New engine-drawn UI for scene projects (Scene settings → UI: Engine). Panels, text, images, buttons, bars, sliders, toggles and scrolling lists are drawn by the engine in every player, so they look the same in the editor, the web export, the C++ players and on Xbox.
- Row and column layout with gaps, alignment and grow. Text wraps to the width it's given, and maxLines adds an ellipsis.
- Gradients, rounded corners, borders, shadows, ring bars, gradient-filled text, and SVG art straight from markup (`{ markup: '<svg…>' }`).
- Controller focus works on everything, and B goes back. UI.zoom sets the interface size, and the in-game safe-area setting works on TVs.
- Handles let a script change a label's text or a bar's value without rebuilding it, and UI.Animate moves, scales, fades and turns items.

## Scene projects
- Font assets (.ttf, .otf, .woff) in project folders work for UI text in every player.
- Native plugins work in scene projects: WebAssembly in the editor and browsers, native code in the C++ players.
- Engine.customRender lets a game draw its own 3D view (post-processing, split screen). The UI is still drawn on top.
- Scenes get the three.js add-ons (sky, post-processing passes, colour grade) in the web export and the C++ player.

## C#
- Members of `dynamic` and `object` values can be set (`o.x = 1`, `o.n++`, `o.v += 2`).
- `new` works on a class from another script.
- A field named like an operator (for example `open`) no longer breaks the build.

## Also in this release
- Everything from 2.26.3: faster starts, compressed textures, quality presets by console.
